LaTeX rendering

Source: vignettes/articles/latex.Rmd
latex.Rmd
library(multimod)

Every node of a model renders as LaTeX with as_latex(), and write_latex() assembles a complete document: sets, parameters, variables, mappings and equations, with the data summarized and the folded or trimmed parts annotated. The examples use the small model built in the Writing a model in R article.

toy <- example_models$toy

Equations and expressions 

as_latex(toy$equations$eqDemand)
#> [1] "\\begin{flushleft}\n\\subsection*{\\textbf{eqDemand} -- \\textit{demand is met in every region}} \n\\quad$\\textbf{eqDemand} \n_{\\texttt{region}}$ \n$\\mid\\left\\{\\texttt{region}\\right\\} \\in \\mathit{mR}_{\\texttt{region}}$ \\\\\n\\begin{equation*}\n\\begin{adjustbox}{max width=\\textwidth}\n$\\begin{aligned}\n&\\sum_{\\texttt{tech}} \\bm{\\mathit{vGen}}_{\\texttt{tech},\\texttt{region}} \\ge \\mathsf{pDemand}_{\\texttt{region}} \\\\\n\\end{aligned}$\n\\end{adjustbox}\n\\end{equation*}\n\\vspace{1em}\n\\end{flushleft}"
as_latex(toy$equations$eqCost$rhs)
#> [1] "\\sum_{\\texttt{tech}, \\texttt{region}} \\mathsf{pCapCost}_{\\texttt{tech}}  \\cdot  \\bm{\\mathit{vCap}}_{\\texttt{tech},\\texttt{region}}  +  \\mathsf{pVarCost}_{\\texttt{tech}}  \\cdot  \\bm{\\mathit{vGen}}_{\\texttt{tech},\\texttt{region}}"

Index aliases shorten the subscripts. The toy carries them already (add_index_aliases() adds them to a model built in R); write_latex() uses them in equations by default and spells the full set names in the declarations.

unlist(toy$index_aliases)
#>   tech region 
#>    "h"    "r"

A document

write_latex() returns the LaTeX source as a character vector and, with file =, writes it.

tex <- write_latex(toy)
length(tex)
#> [1] 1
cat(tex[grep("\\\\section", tex)], sep = "\n")
#> \documentclass{article}
#> \usepackage[letterpaper,margin=1in]{geometry}
#> \usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}

Compiled, the same subsections appear typeset:

Arguments select the sections and the amount of data shown:

tex_eq <- write_latex(toy,
  include_sets = FALSE, include_parameters = FALSE,
  include_variables = FALSE, include_mappings = FALSE,
  include_index_aliases = FALSE
)
length(tex_eq)
#> [1] 1

tex_theory <- write_latex(toy, include_data = FALSE)
length(tex_theory)
#> [1] 1
  • include_data adds set members and parameter row counts; data_detail = "detailed" lists more of each.
  • set_display_max_inline, set_display_head_tail_threshold, set_display_head_n and set_display_tail_n control how long sets are abbreviated.
  • use_aliases_in_declarations = TRUE uses the short indices in the declarations as well; alias_map supplies custom aliases.
  • include_toc, title, subtitle and author shape the document; preamble and ending replace the default wrapper.

Folded and trimmed models

A model that has been through fold_model() or trim_model() (see Folding and trimming) renders in two views. model_view = "reduced", the default for such a model, shows the model as it will be solved; model_view = "full" shows the original declarations with the folded parameters marked in folded_color and the trimmed symbols in trimmed_color, plus a summary of what folding and trimming did.

m <- example_models$energyRt$multimod
mt <- trim_model(m, verbose = FALSE)
get_trim_summary(mt, format = "text")
#> [1] "Model Trimming Summary\n======================\nsets: 6/27 trimmed (22.2%), 21 remaining\nparameters: 1/218 trimmed (0.5%), 217 remaining\nmappings: 160/324 trimmed (49.4%), 164 remaining\nvariables: 10/93 trimmed (10.8%), 83 remaining\nequations: 103/153 trimmed (67.3%), 50 remaining"
tex_full <- write_latex(mt, model_view = "full", trimmed_color = "gray")
sum(grepl("textcolor\\{gray\\}", tex_full))
#> [1] 1

Compiling

The source compiles with pdflatex or xelatex. Its preamble loads geometry, amsmath, amssymb, breqn, graphicx, longtable, adjustbox, multicol, bm, eucal and tikz; \textcolor for trimmed elements comes from xcolor, which tikz loads.

write_latex(toy, file = "toy.tex")
system2("pdflatex", "toy.tex")

The snapshot above is page 2 of that PDF, regenerated with:

write_latex(toy, file = "toy.tex", title = "Model: toy",
            subtitle = "two-region capacity expansion toy model",
            author = "multimod")
tinytex::latexmk("toy.tex", engine = "pdflatex")
page <- magick::image_trim(magick::image_read_pdf("toy.pdf", density = 300)[2])
page <- magick::image_crop(page, paste0(magick::image_info(page)$width, "x1200+0+0"))
magick::image_write(magick::image_border(magick::image_trim(page), "white", "24x24"),
                    "images/toy-latex-rendered.png")

Underscores in symbol names are escaped, and use_latex_names = TRUE (the default) renders names such as pCapCost in upright math. Set it to FALSE to keep every name verbatim.
